data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":["reasoning-envelope-wf"],"disanalogies":["Logs are often private or proprietary, unlike open-source projects.","Stakeholders may lack the technical expertise to verify the log.","Social contracts are not legally enforceable in all contexts."],"overturn_conditions":["A technical binding is proven to be more reliable than social consensus.","The log's structure is shown to be inherently unverifiable by stakeholders.","The definition of 'silent divergence' is redefined to exclude social contradictions."],"shared_structure":["Open-source software development (e.g., GitHub pull requests, peer review).","Scientific peer review (e.g., reproducibility, replication studies).","Contradiction arises from social consensus (e.g., rejected pull request, retracted paper)."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_002","SRC_003"],"transfer_claims":["If peer review prevents scientific fraud, it can prevent log divergence.","If open-source communities detect bugs, they can detect log divergence.","If social consensus enforces norms, it can enforce log consistency."]},"claim":"The durable binding is **a social contract enforced by a decentralized network of stakeholders**, where divergence is treated as a breach of trust.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The network lacks sufficient diversity or independence among stakeholders.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Stakeholders lack the incentives or resources to verify the log.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The log is too large or complex for decentralized verification.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The published result is not publicly accessible for replay.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A decentralized network (e.g., scientific community, open-source project contributors) collectively maintains and verifies the log.
